scores.claim_text: Planet operates Planet Labs Federal, Inc., a subsidiary headquartered in a 3,000 sq ft Washington, D.C. office, serving as the corporate headquarters for U.S. federal/defense engagement.
scores.interpretation: Planet Labs Federal, Inc. is a real federally-registered entity (UEI TFCJCMKNHT74). Filing says 'Washington, D.C.' but registered physical address is Arlington, VA — cosmetic, immaterial. usaspending confirms RECURRING_FEDERAL with $82.3M lifetime federal awards across 61 contracts. Federal channel is real.

scores.claim_text: Planet expects 'Defense & Intelligence' to be a significant market driver via sharable, unclassified subscription products — forward narrative without naming a specific Pentagon program.

M_value.by_entity_corpus_hits: Planet Labs is NOT among the 58 J-Book entities mapped in by_entity.json

scores.interpretation: Forward-looking and DELIBERATELY VAGUE — Planet names no Program Element, no PE number, no named program (Maven/EOCL/TCPED/Tactical GEOINT), no contract vehicle. Per heuristic 7 (NOT_FOUND != red flag), the J-Book divergence pattern cannot trigger because the company never gave a specific program to verify. Itself a finding: the J-Book Exposure Divergence pattern requires named-program-revenue claims; PL's FY22 10-K is structurally immune because defense exposure is sold as a category, not as named programs. ABSENCE OF DISCLOSURE rather than UNDERDELIVERY.

scores.claim_text: Planet operates a fleet of ~200 satellites including 21 SkySat high-resolution agile-tasking satellites, providing the backbone for tasking-based revenue (including federal tasking).

usaspending_top_award_descriptions: EARTH OBSERVATIONS FROM PRIVATE SECTOR SMALL SATELITE CONSTELLATIONS PILOT ($7.0M)
PRIVATE SECTOR SMALL CONSTELLATION SATELLITE DATA PRODUCT PILOT ($6.7M)
COMMERCIAL SMALLSAT DATA ACQUISITION PROGRAM - PLANETSCOPE AND RAPIDEYE DATA PURCHASE ($6.2M x2)

scores.interpretation: Fleet existence (SkySat + Dove constellation) is independently corroborated by NASA's CSDAP and SmallSat constellation pilots, which contract for PlanetScope/RapidEye/SkySat data. Satellite-fleet claim verifies; J-Book corpus lacks the underlying Commercial Satellite Imagery / EOCL line item but this is corpus-coverage gap, not a divergence.

scores.claim_text: Planet's forward strategy depends on continuing to capture 'certain high-value government procurement contracts'.
scores.interpretation: Past federal presence is real ($82M, 61 awards). But 'high-value government procurement contracts' is unspecified — no PE, no program of record, no named contract vehicle (e.g., EOCL/Tactical GEOINT/TPED). Forward dependency cannot be verified or falsified at the program level. Note: heaviest agency by count is NASA (18 contracts), not DoD (7) — narrative emphasis on 'Defense & Intelligence' overweights actual DoD share of the federal book at cutoff.

NASA channel is real (18 contracts including CSDAP). Hyperspectral partnership claim is internally consistent and not contradicted; PASS.
